description: Transcribe a document that holds no readable text: a scanned PDF, a photographed page, or a deck whose content is pictures. Renders the pages that need it and reads them with a vision model, so it costs money per page — pass `pages` (pdf::classify names them) to narrow it. Needs the browser worker for PDFs and a vision model through llm-router.

FsScope.description:
The filesystem jail a call runs under.

The harness stamps this onto every function it dispatches, so a `path` an agent supplies has to be checked against it. Without the check these functions would read any document on the machine and hand back its text, which is a way around the scope the session was granted. Mirrors the shape the shell and pdf workers take.

grants.description: Additional directories or files explicitly granted to this session.

request_schema.description: Where the document comes from. Exactly one of `path` and `bytes_base64` must be set.

bytes_base64.description: Base64-encoded document bytes, for a document with no path — an attachment held in memory. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

file_name.description: Original file name for inline bytes, used only to recognise a format the content cannot name. A `.csv` needs this; nothing else does. Ignored when `path` is set, which carries its own name.

fs_scope.description: The filesystem jail this call runs under. Stamped by the harness on an agent's call; absent on an operator or console call, which is already user-initiated and not subject to the agent's scope.

max_chars.description: Characters to return before truncating. Omit for the configured default; `0` returns everything transcribed.

model.description: Vision model to read with. Omit for the configured default. The model is checked for vision support before anything is rendered.

pages.description: 1-indexed pages to transcribe, for a PDF. Omit for every page up to the configured ceiling. This is the cost control: `pdf::classify` reports which pages are scans, and passing that list keeps a long report from being read a page at a time when only its cover is an image.

path.description: Filesystem path to the document. Mutually exclusive with `bytes_base64`.

request_schema.title: Request

Body.description:
A body that may have been shortened to fit one response, and the numbers a caller needs to decide what to do about it.

The cap is what keeps a long document from flooding a model's context. A caller that genuinely wants the whole thing asks for `max_chars: 0`, which is the shape a worker-to-worker pipeline uses to move a document without it passing through anyone's context. Same shape the pdf worker returns, so a caller handling both reads one field set.

preview.description: Leading characters of the content. Present only when the body was truncated, so a caller can see the shape of what it did not get without re-reading the start of `text`.

text.description: The markdown, shortened to the effective character cap.

total_chars.description: Characters the document actually holds. Equal to `chars` when nothing was dropped.

truncated.description: `true` when `text` stops short of the document. Ask again with `max_chars: 0` to take everything.

cached.description: `true` when this page came from the cache rather than the model.

page.description: 1-indexed page number, or the asset's index for an office document.

text.description: The transcription. Empty when the page held no legible text.

pages_cached.description: Pages served from the cache, costing nothing.

pages_transcribed.description: Pages actually read by the model this call. Excludes cache hits, so this is what was paid for.

source.description: Source label: the file name, or `<inline>` for an in-memory document.

via.description: How the pixels were obtained: `image`, `pdf-render` or `document-assets`.
